about: The evangelium of the formulary “4th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, when the crowds were thronging Jesus to hear the word of God, He Himself was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret. And He saw two boats standing beside the lake; but the fishermen had disembarked and were washing the nets. And going aboard one of the boats, which belonged to Simon, He asked him to pull back a little from the shore. And sitting down, He was teaching the crowds out of the boat. And when He had stopped speaking, He said to Simon: Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch. And in answer Simon said to Him: Master, we toiled through the whole night and caught nothing; yet at Your word I will let down the net. And having done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their net began to tear. And they signaled to their partners in the other boat that they should come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that they were almost sinking. Seeing this, Simon Peter fell down at the knees of Jesus, saying: Go away from me, because I am a sinful man, Lord. For astonishment had seized him and all who were with him at the haul of fish which they had taken; and likewise James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s partners. And Jesus said to Simon: Have no fear; from now on you will be catching men. And when they had drawn their boats up on land, they left everything and followed Him.
